sections.title: Top bar
sections.intro: The strip across the top is always visible. It starts and stops the loop, sets the tempo, and opens the Library, the Assistant and this Guide.

marks.name: Play / Stop
marks.text: Starts the loop from the beginning, or stops it. On a PC keyboard, Space does the same.

marks.name: Record
marks.text: Starts the loop if it is stopped, then writes every pad you hit into the loop. Press it again to stop recording while the loop keeps playing. One Undo removes the whole take.

marks.name: Click
marks.text: Turns the metronome on or off. It is never included in an export.

marks.name: Position
marks.text: Shows the bar and beat while the loop plays.

marks.name: Tempo
marks.text: Type a tempo from 40 to 240 BPM, or nudge it with the − and + buttons on either side. Tempo can change while the loop plays.

marks.name: Tap
marks.text: Tap along to a beat three or more times to set the tempo by feel.

marks.name: Loop length
marks.text: The loop is 1, 2 or 4 bars long. Step patterns repeat every bar; recorded hits and piano-roll notes can sit anywhere in the loop. Shortening the loop removes what no longer fits.

marks.name: Snap
marks.text: While recording, each hit is pulled to the nearest 1/8, 1/16 or 1/32 note. Off keeps your exact timing.

marks.name: Undo / Redo
marks.text: Step back through anything that changed the project: cuts, pad sends, patterns, effects, takes, and everything the Assistant did in one reply.

marks.name: Export
marks.text: Renders one pass of the loop to an audio file. Echo and reverb tails that run past the end are wrapped to the start, so the file loops cleanly. Inside the Claude page the WAV arrives in a zip.

marks.name: Library
marks.text: Opens your saved sounds and saved projects.

marks.name: Assistant
marks.text: Opens the chat panel. The Assistant can read your pads and change the studio for you.

marks.name: Guide
marks.text: Opens these instructions.

marks.name: Status
marks.text: The number is the sound delay your device reports, in milliseconds; lower feels tighter. Next to it: saved, saving, or not saving if the browser is blocking storage.

sections.title: Module tabs
sections.intro: One tab for every tool in the workstation. The Sampler is where everything built so far lives. Tabs marked soon are tools that are planned but not built yet; each opens a page saying what it will do, where it is in the build order, and what you can do today instead.

marks.name: Sampler
marks.text: The working studio: chop view, piano roll, pads, steps and effects.

marks.name: Clips
marks.text: Save loops as clips and launch them live, in time with each other.

marks.name: Arrange
marks.text: Lay clips along a timeline to build a full song, then export it.

marks.name: Mixer
marks.text: A channel strip for each pad bank with level, pan, EQ, mute, solo and meters.

marks.name: Analyze
marks.text: Suggested loops, drum hits and vocal or lead lines from a whole song, ready to send to pads.

marks.name: Stems
marks.text: Planned: split a song into vocals, drums, bass and the rest.

marks.name: Suno
marks.text: Build a Suno style and lyrics, generate, and browse your Suno library.

marks.name: AI setup
marks.text: Planned: run the Assistant on Google Gemini, GPT or your own PC, and give it your documents.

marks.name: Plugins
marks.text: Planned for the desktop version: VST and CLAP plugins.

sections.title: Chop view
sections.intro: This is where a track becomes playable pieces. Bring audio in, cut it into slices, and send the slices to the pads.

marks.name: Chop / Piano roll
marks.text: Switches the top area between cutting up audio and writing notes for the selected pad.

marks.name: Import audio
marks.text: Choose a WAV or MP3 from your device. It is added to the project and shown here.

marks.name: Sample menu
marks.text: Every sample in the project. Pick which one the chop view shows.

marks.name: Use detected tempo
marks.text: Appears when a tempo was detected in the sample. Tap to set the project to it. Very fast or slow tracks can read as half or double; type the right number if so.

marks.name: Save to library
marks.text: Keeps the whole sample in your Library so other projects can use it.

marks.name: Waveform tool
marks.text: Audition: tap a slice to hear it. Add cut: tap the waveform to place a cut. Remove cut: tap a cut to delete it. In any tool you can drag a yellow cut marker to move it.

marks.name: Auto-slice
marks.text: Places cuts at the hits it finds in the audio. The slider next to it sets how sensitive it is: move right for more slices.

marks.name: Equal cuts
marks.text: ÷8 and ÷16 cut the sample into equal parts. Best for a loop that is exactly a number of bars long.

marks.name: Clear cuts
marks.text: Removes every cut so the sample is one slice again.

marks.name: Send to pads
marks.text: Puts the slices on the pads, starting at pad 1 of the bank on screen and running into the next banks if there are more than 16. The count beside it tells you how many slices there are.

marks.name: Waveform
marks.text: Each slice is tinted with the colour of the pad it will land on and labelled with that pad's name. Yellow lines are the cuts.

marks.name: Zoom
marks.text: + zooms in for precise cuts on long tracks; − zooms out. When zoomed in, a slider appears under the waveform to scroll.

sections.title: Pads and banks
sections.intro: Sixteen pads on screen, four banks deep: 64 pads in all. Pad 1 is bottom-left, like a hardware sampler.

marks.name: Banks A to D
marks.text: Switch which 16 pads are on screen. A dot marks a bank that has sounds on it. All banks keep playing in the loop, whichever one you are looking at.

marks.name: A pad
marks.text: Tap to play it and select it. A coloured pad has a sound; a grey pad is empty. Pads glow when they play, including when the loop plays them.

marks.name: Selected pad
marks.text: The white outline shows which pad the Steps, Pad and FX tabs and the piano roll are working on.

notes: On a PC keyboard the pads are on Z X C V (bottom row), A S D F, Q W E R and 1 2 3 4 (top row). The keys play the bank on screen and are switched off while you type in a text box.

sections.title: Steps tab
sections.intro: A step sequencer for the selected pad. The 16 steps are the 16th notes of one bar, and the pattern repeats every bar of the loop.

marks.name: Tabs
marks.text: Steps, Pad and FX all act on the selected pad. A dot after FX means that pad has effects switched on.

marks.name: A step
marks.text: Tap once for a full hit, again for a soft hit, again for off. Steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 have a brighter edge: those are the beats. A white ring moves across while the loop plays.

marks.name: Swing
marks.text: Delays every second 16th note for a looser feel. It applies to the whole project. Around 16 to 25% is a classic swing.

marks.name: Clear steps
marks.text: Empties this pad's step pattern.

marks.name: Erase recorded hits
marks.text: Removes the hits you recorded live on this pad, leaving its steps alone.

marks.name: Erase all recorded
marks.text: Removes live-recorded hits on every pad.

sections.title: Pad tab
sections.intro: The basic settings of the selected pad.

marks.name: Pitch
marks.text: Up or down 12 semitones. Like a classic sampler, lower is also slower and higher is faster. To change length without pitch, use Stretch in the FX tab.

marks.name: Reverse
marks.text: Plays the slice backwards.

marks.name: ◀ Slice / Slice ▶
marks.text: Moves the pad to the previous or next slice of the same sample, for when a pad landed one slice off.

marks.name: Save to library
marks.text: Saves this pad exactly as it sounds, with its pitch and effects, as a one-shot in your Library.

marks.name: Clear pad
marks.text: Empties the pad, along with its steps, recorded hits and notes.

sections.title: FX tab
sections.intro: Effects for the selected pad only. Every pad has its own. What you hear is exactly what is exported.

marks.name: Filter
marks.text: Low-pass removes highs (darker). High-pass removes lows (thinner). Band-pass keeps a band in the middle (telephone-like).

marks.name: Cutoff and Resonance
marks.text: Cutoff is where the filter acts. Resonance adds a ringing peak at that point. Both appear when a filter is on.

marks.name: Drive
marks.text: Saturation. Low settings add warmth, the middle gets crunchy, the top is destroyed.

marks.name: Echo
marks.text: How loud the echoes are. The original sound stays at full level.

marks.name: Echo time and Repeats
marks.text: Time is locked to the tempo: 1/16, 1/8, dotted 1/8 or 1/4 note. Repeats sets how long the echoes carry on.

marks.name: Reverb
marks.text: How much of the pad goes into a space. 15 to 40% is normal; 100% is a wash.

marks.name: Space
marks.text: Room is short and tight, Hall is about two seconds, Vast is five.

marks.name: Stretch
marks.text: Makes the slice longer or shorter without changing its pitch.

marks.sel: [aria-label="Stretch the slice to a musical length"]
marks.name: Fit to
marks.text: Stretches the slice to exactly a quarter note, half note, one bar or two bars at the current tempo. A button is greyed out when the slice would have to stretch more than four times or shrink below a quarter.

marks.name: Scatter and Grain size
marks.text: Scatter makes tiny pieces of the slice jump around, turning a hit or a voice into a texture. Grain size sets how long those pieces are: shorter is cleaner on drums, longer is smoother on held sounds.

marks.name: Stutter
marks.text: Repeats the first part of the slice ×2 to ×8 in the time the whole slice would take.

marks.name: Hear it
marks.text: Plays the pad without leaving the panel.

marks.name: Remove effects
marks.text: Switches every effect on this pad off.

marks.name: Resample
marks.text: Prints the pad with its pitch and effects into a brand-new sample and points the pad at it with the effects cleared. The new sample is in the sample menu, ready to be chopped again or given more effects.

sections.title: Piano roll and MIDI
sections.intro: The piano roll plays the selected pad's sound at other pitches, so one note can become a bassline, a melody or chords. Pads holding a single clear note work best.

marks.name: Piano roll
marks.text: Switches the top area to the piano roll for the selected pad. Select a different pad to write for a different sound.

marks.name: Scale
marks.text: Only the notes of this scale get a row, so every row is a right note. Choose Chromatic to see every semitone.

marks.name: Pad is
marks.text: The note name of the pad's own pitch. It labels the rows and lines MIDI files up with the real key.

marks.name: Length
marks.text: How long a new note is when you tap.

marks.name: Clear notes
marks.text: Removes every note on this pad.

marks.name: Import MIDI
marks.text: Reads a MIDI file's notes onto this pad. Notes too high or low are moved by octaves into range; notes past the end of the loop are left out, and you are told how many.

marks.name: Export MIDI
marks.text: Saves the loop as a MIDI file: pad patterns and recorded hits on the drum channel, and a track for each pad that has notes.

marks.name: Connect keyboard
marks.text: Shown where the browser supports MIDI devices. With the piano roll open the keys play the selected pad; in Chop view, notes 36 to 51 hit the 16 pads. Recording captures what you play.

marks.name: The roll
marks.text: Tap a square to add a note. Drag right while adding to make it longer. Tap a note to remove it. Tap a note name on the left to hear that pitch. The row marked ● is the pad's own pitch. Notes go through the pad's effects.

sections.title: Clips
sections.intro: A clip is a saved loop. Make a pattern in the Sampler, save it here, change the pattern, save again. Then launch clips on different tracks and they play together, in time. While this page is open the transport plays clips; everywhere else it plays the Sampler loop.

marks.name: A track
marks.text: Four tracks. One clip plays per track at a time; launching another on the same track replaces it on the next bar.

marks.name: M, S and ■
marks.text: M mutes the track. S solos it, silencing the others. ■ stops the track's clip at the next bar line.

marks.name: Volume
marks.text: How loud this track's clips play.

marks.name: A clip
marks.text: Tap to launch. It flashes while it waits for the next bar line, then lights up and shows ▶ while it plays. Tap a playing clip to stop it.

marks.name: Clip options
marks.text: Edit in Sampler puts the clip back into the Sampler loop so you can change it and save it again. Rename and Delete are here too.

marks.name: Save Sampler loop here
marks.text: Saves what the Sampler loop holds right now (steps, recorded hits and piano-roll notes) as a new clip on this track.

notes: Clips remember the pattern, not the sounds: they play whatever is on the pads now, with the pads' current effects. Record is switched off on this page because recording writes into the Sampler loop.

sections.title: Arrange
sections.intro: Turn clips into a song. Each row is one of the four clip tracks and each column is a bar. While this page is open, Play runs the song from the chosen bar and stops at the end.

marks.name: Clip to place
marks.text: Every clip you have saved. Tap one to choose it. The label shows its track and length.

marks.name: Bar numbers
marks.text: Tap a bar number to choose where Play starts. The yellow number is the start bar.

marks.name: A track row
marks.text: Tap an empty bar to place the chosen clip there. A clip always lands on its own track, and two clips cannot overlap on one track.

marks.name: A placed clip
marks.text: Tap it to select it. The thin lines inside show where the clip repeats.

marks.name: Move
marks.text: Slides the selected clip one bar earlier or later.

marks.name: Repeat
marks.text: Makes the selected clip play more or fewer times in a row.

marks.name: Remove
marks.text: Takes the selected clip off the timeline. The clip itself stays on the Clips page.

marks.name: Clear timeline
marks.text: Removes everything from the timeline. Undo brings it back.

marks.name: Export song
marks.text: Renders the whole song to an audio file, with a few seconds at the end for echoes and reverb to fade. The length beside it is the song so far.

notes: Track volume, mute and solo are set on the Clips page and apply here too.

sections.title: Mixer
sections.intro: One channel strip for each bank of pads, plus a master. Everything on bank A goes through strip A, wherever it plays: the Sampler loop, Clips or Arrange. The mixer is part of every export.

marks.name: High, Mid, Low
marks.text: Tone controls. Turn High down to soften harsh hats, Low down to clean up a muddy bank, Mid up to bring a vocal forward. Double-tap a slider to put it back to 0.

marks.name: Pan
marks.text: Places the bank left or right. Centre is normal; spreading banks a little apart makes a mix feel wider.

marks.name: Fader
marks.text: The bank's level. Drag up or down. Double-tap to go back to 0 dB.

marks.name: Meter
marks.text: How loud the bank is right now. Green is fine, yellow is loud, red means it is too hot.

marks.name: Mute and Solo
marks.text: Mute silences the bank. Solo plays only the soloed banks, so you can hear one part on its own.

marks.name: Master
marks.text: The level of everything together. If its meter hits red, pull the bank faders down rather than the master.

marks.name: Reset mixer
marks.text: Puts every strip back to flat and centred. Undo brings your settings back.

notes: Clips tracks have their own volume, mute and solo on the Clips page; they are separate from the bank strips here. Pads saved to the Library or resampled are printed without the mixer, so a muted bank does not end up as a silent sample.

sections.title: Analyze
sections.intro: The quickest way to turn a downloaded song into pads. Pick the song, tap Analyse, listen to the suggestions, tick the ones you like, and send them to a bank.

marks.name: Import a song
marks.text: Brings a WAV or MP3 into the project and selects it for analysis.

marks.name: Song
marks.text: Which sample in the project to analyse.

marks.name: Analyse
marks.text: Measures the song. A long song can take a few seconds. Only the first six minutes are analysed.

marks.name: Use tempo
marks.text: Sets the project to the song's tempo, so loops from it play in time.

marks.name: Overview
marks.text: The whole song, with each suggestion marked: loops on the top row, vocal or lead lines in the middle, hits at the bottom. Ticked ones are brighter.

marks.name: Loops
marks.text: Stretches of 1, 2 or 4 bars that repeat cleanly, counted from the beat. The percentage says how closely the next bars match.

marks.name: Hits
marks.text: The strongest single drum hits, labelled by their tone: low (kick or bass), mid (snare or clap) or bright (hat or shaker).

marks.name: Vocal or lead lines
marks.text: Places where a steady pitch holds for a while, which is usually singing. It measures pitch, not words, so a lead synth can show up here too.

marks.name: Play and tick
marks.text: ▶ plays the suggestion. The tick box chooses it for sending.

marks.name: Send to bank
marks.text: Which bank the ticked suggestions go to, starting at pad 1. It replaces what is on that bank; the note beside it warns you how many pads are loaded.

marks.name: Send to pads
marks.text: Puts the ticked suggestions on the pads, up to 16. One Undo takes them all off again.

sections.title: Suno
sections.intro: Write better Suno prompts and keep your Suno work next to your samples. The builder works everywhere. Generating, the queue and your Suno library work when the studio is opened in Claude with the Suno connector.

marks.name: Title
marks.text: Optional. Suno makes one up if you leave it empty.

marks.name: The seven parts
marks.text: Describe the sound piece by piece: era, key and mood, tempo, voice, lead instruments, drums and low end, and how it is mixed. Tap a suggestion under a box to add it, or type your own. Be specific: “rubbery 303 acid line” beats “synth”.

marks.name: Style sent to Suno
marks.text: The seven parts joined together, ready to send. Edit by hand lets you rewrite it freely; Rebuild puts it back. Copy puts it on the clipboard for pasting into Suno itself.

marks.name: Keep out
marks.text: Sounds Suno should avoid. Use it for whatever generic thing a take keeps drifting towards.

marks.name: Section tags
marks.text: Tap to insert [Verse], [Chorus], [Drop] and the rest at the cursor, each on its own line.

marks.name: Lyrics
marks.text: Up to 5000 characters. Tick Instrumental to make a song with no vocals.

marks.name: Generate
marks.text: Model, voice, and three sliders: Weirdness (how far it strays), Style strength (how closely it follows your style) and Variety (how freely it reinterprets it). Leave a slider alone to let Suno decide. Generate asks you to confirm first, because it makes 2 songs and spends your Suno credits.

notes: Queue: new songs appear here and update by themselves. Open in Suno plays them on suno.com. Get WAV asks Suno for a download link; if that needs one of your download credits, it asks you first.
Your Suno library: search your songs, open them, download them, or tap Use its style to load a song's style into the builder and change it.

Getting sounds between Suno and the studio takes one extra step each way, because the studio page cannot fetch files from Suno: download from Suno, then use Import audio. To send a loop to Suno, export it, tap Start upload, pick the file on Suno's page, then tap Done.
The Assistant can fill in the builder for you: ask it to write a Suno prompt for the track you are making. It never generates; you review and press Generate.

sections.title: Library: sounds
sections.intro: Sounds you save stay in this browser between sessions and can go into any project.

marks.name: Sounds / Projects
marks.text: Switch between saved sounds and saved projects.

marks.name: Add audio files
marks.text: Add one or many files straight into the Library without putting them in the project.

marks.name: Save current loop
marks.text: Renders the loop that is playing now and saves it as a sound.

marks.name: Search
marks.text: Filters by name or tag. The tag buttons beside it filter with one tap.

marks.name: Preview
marks.text: Plays the sound. Tap again to stop.

marks.name: To chop view
marks.text: Adds the sound to the project and shows it in the chop view for cutting.

marks.name: To pad
marks.text: Puts the whole sound on the selected pad. Select the pad you want before opening the Library.

marks.name: Rename / tag
marks.text: Change the name and add tags, separated by commas, such as kick, vocal, dark.

marks.name: Download
marks.text: Saves the sound to your device.

marks.name: Delete
marks.text: Tap twice to remove the sound from the Library. Projects that already use it are not affected.

notes: Other ways in: Save to library in the chop view saves the whole sample, and Save to library on the Pad tab saves one pad exactly as it sounds.
The Library lives in this browser on this device. Clearing the browser's site data removes it, so download anything you cannot afford to lose.

sections.title: Library: projects
sections.intro: What is on screen is always autosaved. Save it under a name to keep it while you start something else.

marks.name: Project name
marks.text: Type a name for what is on screen now.

marks.name: Save project
marks.text: Saves it. Using a name that already exists updates that project.

marks.name: Open
marks.text: Tap twice. It replaces what is on screen, so save first if you want to keep it.

marks.name: Delete
marks.text: Tap twice to remove the saved project.

sections.title: Assistant
sections.intro: A producer in a chat panel that can operate the studio. It cannot hear, so it measures each pad to tell a kick from a hat, and says when it is unsure.

marks.name: Starters
marks.text: Tap one to send it, or use them as examples of what to ask.

marks.name: Message box
marks.text: Ask in your own words: build a beat from these pads, write a phrygian bassline on A4, put a dark low-pass and dotted echo on A3, how do I get a less generic sound out of Suno. Enter sends; Shift+Enter makes a new line.

marks.name: Send / Stop
marks.text: Sends the message. While it is working this becomes Stop.

marks.name: Close
marks.text: Hides the panel. The conversation is kept until you start a new chat or reload the page.

notes: Each change it makes is listed with a tick. Under its reply, Undo these changes takes back everything from that reply in one tap.
In the Claude page it runs on your own Claude account and asks permission the first time. On the web link it needs an Anthropic API key, which stays in that browser.

workflows.title: Chop a track onto pads
steps: Tap Import audio and choose a WAV or MP3.
Tap Auto-slice. Move the slider beside it until the cuts sit on the hits you want.
Fix any cut by dragging its yellow marker, or switch the tool to Add cut or Remove cut.
Tap Send to pads.
Tap the pads to play your slices.

workflows.title: Turn a downloaded song into pads
steps: Open Analyze and tap Import a song.
Tap Analyse.
Tap ▶ on suggestions to hear them. Tick the ones you like.
Choose a bank and tap Send to pads.
Open the Sampler, switch to that bank and play. Shape the sounds on the FX tab.

workflows.title: Get a less generic sound from Suno
steps: Open the Suno tab.
Fill the seven parts with specific sounds, not genres: tap the suggestions to start.
Add the stock sounds you keep getting to Keep out.
Generate, listen in Suno, and keep the best take.
Download it, Import it here, Analyze or chop it, reshape it on the FX tab, and export your own loop.
Send that loop back to Suno with Start upload, and use it in your next song.

workflows.title: Record a loop
steps: Set the tempo, loop length and Snap in the top bar.
Turn on Click if you want a metronome.
Tap Record. The loop starts.
Play the pads. Each hit comes back the next time round.
Tap Record again to stop recording, or Stop to end. One Undo removes the whole take.

workflows.title: Program a beat with steps
steps: Tap the pad you want, for example your kick.
On the Steps tab, tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.
Tap another pad and give it its own steps. Tap a step twice for a soft hit.
Press Play and adjust while it loops. Add Swing to loosen it.

workflows.title: Build a song from clips
steps: Make a drum pattern in the Sampler.
Open Clips and tap Save Sampler loop here on Track 1.
Go back to the Sampler, clear the drums, and make a bassline or melody.
Open Clips and save it on Track 2.
Open Arrange. Tap a clip at the top, then tap bars on the timeline to place it. Use + Repeat to make sections longer.
Press Play to hear the song, then Export song.

workflows.title: Turn one note into a bassline
steps: Find a slice that is one clear note and tap its pad.
Switch the top area to Piano roll.
Pick a scale. Set Pad is to the note's name if you know it.
Tap squares to place notes; drag right for longer ones.
Press Play. Open the FX tab to shape the sound.

workflows.title: Make a loop fit the tempo
steps: Put the loop on a pad as one slice.
Open the FX tab.
Under Fit to, tap the length it should last: 1/4, 1/2, Bar or 2 bars.
If it sounds grainy, change Grain size: shorter for drums, longer for held sounds.

workflows.title: Design a new sound and reuse it
steps: Pick a pad and open the FX tab.
Stack effects: try Stretch ×4, Scatter and a Vast reverb on a vocal fragment.
Tap Resample. The pad now plays the printed result.
Switch to Chop view: the resampled sound is in the sample menu. Cut it up and send the pieces to another bank.
Tap Save to library on the Pad tab to keep the best ones.

workflows.title: Save and share your work
steps: Tap Export in the top bar for an audio file of the loop.
For a full song, open Arrange and tap Export song.
In Piano roll view, tap Export MIDI for the notes and patterns.
Open the Library, go to Projects, type a name and tap Save project to keep the whole session.

shortcuts: Send a message to the Assistant
New line in the Assistant box
